rendered:
The premise is not what the paper says. It does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]. It concludes the opposite. The paper states that its work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[2], which it says will increase energy density and decrease the cost of Li-ion batteries.

On lithium leaching, the paper says that although leached Li+ rises with nickel content, even Ni-rich NMC 811[3] shows only minimal leaching, about ~3 wt%[4] after a week. XRD and Raman analysis of the powders after water exposure showed no bulk structural change, so the paper does not treat this leaching as a barrier.

The paper does note a tradeoff: aqueous-processed Ni-rich cells retain slightly less capacity than NMP-processed cells, yet the authors still describe their cycling performance as very good cycling performance[5]. Their caveats concern formulation control, namely Li/H+ exchange in solution, a highly basic solvent pH, and changes to the Ni-rich surface morphology. These are conditions for doing aqueous processing well, not reasons it is incompatible.
